name: Ngongo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: No description of Ngongo (noq) itself found; Glottolog lists only subclassification papers (Pacchiarotti et al. 2019); nearby KiYaka work does not cover Ngongo

sources.citation: Bostoen, Koen, Sara Pacchiarotti & Guy Kouarata. 2025. Language divergence and convergence and deep-time population history in the Kwilu-Kasai region (Routledge OA chapter).
sources.note: Ngong (B864) named only in the KLC-Extended classification; nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437-475.
sources.note: Ngong B864 listed with 'systematic' final vowel loss (Table 1: 9/354 = 2.5% lexemes keep a final vowel; data from Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015); no mention of stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph & Koen Bostoen. 2012. La diphtongaison dans les langues bantu B70-80 (Bandundu, RDC): typologie et classification historique. Africana Linguistica 18: 355-386. doi:10.3406/aflin.2012.1015 (Persée, read page by page; PDF altcha-gated)
sources.note: Ngong B864 is one of 13 languages compared; diphthongs arise only in the first root syllable (p.382); nothing on stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph. 2010. Plantes, animaux et champignons en langues bantu: étude comparée de phytonymes, zoonymes et myconymes en nsong, ngong, mpiin, mbuun et hungan (Bandundu, RD Congo). Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles (dir. K. Bostoen & A. Shango Mutambwe), xii+559 pp. [ULB DI-fusion open scan, handle 2013/210114]
sources.note: Ch.1 gives vowel system (1.1.1.4, p.38-39: six vowels, phonological length and nasality), consonants (1.1.2.4, p.46), 'Système tonal ngong' (1.1.3.4, p.55-56: H, L, rising, falling, all distinctive, every syllable nucleus bears a tone, 'cas tonals' by syntactic position) and syllable structure (1.1.4, p.57). No statement about word stress or accent anywhere in the thesis; 'accent' occurs only as 'accent aigu' = H-tone diacritic (p.51).

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Nsong B85d. In M. Van de Velde, K. Bostoen, D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 2nd ed., 414-448. London: Routledge.
